outcome: Sickle cell disease-related complications during pregnancy
cohort: 48 patients with sickle cell disease who delivered at >20 weeks' gestation at two sites within the University of Pennsylvania Health System from May 1, 2017 to August 30, 2020
finding: Sickle cell disease was associated with significant perinatal morbidity for both mothers and neonates, including high rates of hospital admission during pregnancy, preterm delivery, cesarean delivery, and neonatal intensive care unit admission.
mod_finding: The primary cesarean rate in nulliparas was 43%.
